hook: Banks gave Telangana farmers far less kharif credit than *targeted*
hook_b: Banks gave Telangana farmers far less kharif credit than *targeted*
tldr: Banks in Telangana disbursed ₹96,942 crore of the ₹1.81 lakh crore priority sector lending target in April-September, The Hindu reports, as kharif output fell.

beats.what: Short-term kharif crop-loan targets of ₹58,152 crore were missed, with public sector banks lagging others.
beats.why: Kharif production fell an estimated 16-17% due to an El Niño-linked monsoon deficit.
beats.care: Farmers are being told to avoid paddy in rabi, and there are doubts banks will lend more in the second half.

causes.label: El Niño monsoon deficit cut kharif output

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Private banks disbursed ₹15,140 crore of a ₹21,316 crore target, 71.03%.

cards.q: Should banks face penalties for missing farm-loan targets?

qs: Do farmers turn to moneylenders when bank credit falls short?
Will rabi crop shifts change how much banks lend?

facts.t: Foreign banks disbursed *₹567 crore*, 463% of a ₹122 crore target.
Public sector banks lent *₹62,567 crore* of a ₹1.15 lakh crore yearly target.

viz.verdict: About 54% of the year's target reached, farmers get less credit
Public sector banks lagged private banks

learn.t: Priority sector lending = loans banks must give to farming and other set sectors

watch: Whether banks lend more in the rabi season as farmers shift away from paddy.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Farmers suffer during kharif as banks did not achieve targets of agri credit

fact: Banks hit only *about half* of Telangana's yearly priority-lending target by September
twist: Foreign banks lent 463% of their target, while public sector banks reached about 54%.
